focus.jtag: U.S. hit dozens of Iranian targets overnight, Brent >$91, 30Y yield at 2007 high near 5.24%, Nasdaq in correction
focus.jnote: Two shocks stacked on one tape. First, the war widened overnight: the U.S. struck dozens of Iranian military targets in a two-hour operation after Tehran fired ballistic missiles at a U.S. base in Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Iraq were pulled in, and two LNG vessels caught fire off Egypt — Brent pushed above $91 before easing, WTI near $84–85. Second, the bond market is revolting after Wednesday’s Fed hold: the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest since 2007 near 5.24%, and the Nasdaq entered a correction as chips got crushed (Micron −9.9%, AMD −5.5%). Equity futures nonetheless bounced — S&P futures up ~0.3–0.7%, Nasdaq up ~0.7% — helped by Microsoft’s strong Azure print, even as Meta fell ~9% pre-market. This is a live, open-ended conflict layered on a rate shock — exactly the headline tape a Sniper does not sell premium into. And with Q2 GDP, jobless claims and the PCE inflation gauge all at 8:30 AM, the morning has scheduled macro risk too.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX) and Defense (LMT, RTX, NOC) are the natural war-bid groups — oil-supply fear lifts energy, conflict demand lifts defense. But be honest: these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers. One de-escalation or ceasefire headline gaps them straight back down. Note the scanner boarded zero Type B names today. Watch-only.
focus.notup: Chips / AI-heavy tech (NVDA, MU, AMD) and Meta (−9% pre-market on a weak print and raised capex) stay pressured, and the fundamental lean is lower. But selling bear calls into a VIX near 20, a bond rout, and a war tape carries violent-squeeze risk on any peace or dovish headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 66 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 44% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military exchange with an oil shock plus a 2007-high long bond yield is an unscheduled, open-ended tail — worse than a known event because you cannot time or size around the next headline. On top of that, the scanner flagged that liquidity (ATM spread and open interest) could NOT be verified on any boarded name because TastyTrade was unreachable, and several show thin/absent OI — an independent hard stop. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the conflict window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: Fresh U.S.–Iran strikes — the U.S. hit dozens of Iranian targets overnight after Tehran fired missiles at a base in Jordan; Saudi Arabia and Iraq are drawn in and LNG vessels are ablaze off Egypt. Any hit on personnel gaps the whole tape instantly.

Bond rout — the 30-year Treasury yield hit a multi-decade high near 5.24% after the Fed held rates and Warsh signaled less guidance. A further yield spike compounds pressure on stocks, especially long-duration tech.
8:30 AM data cluster — Q2 GDP first estimate, weekly jobless claims, and the June PCE inflation gauge all land pre-open. A hot PCE on top of an oil shock is the worst-case macro combination.
Strait of Hormuz & oil — Brent topped $91 overnight; roughly a fifth of the world’s oil moves through Hormuz. Any attack or closure sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

Mega-cap tech tonight — AMZN & AAPL — after Meta’s ~9% pre-market drop and Microsoft’s Azure-driven bid, the next hyperscaler prints land tonight with COIN. Single-stock gap risk stacked on a jittery tape.

Liquidity unverifiable today — the scanner could not reach TastyTrade, so ATM spread and OI are unconfirmed on every boarded name, and several show thin/absent OI. This is an independent hard stop before any entry.
